summary: Return the sum of squares of the elements nums[i] (1-indexed) where i divides the length n.
mainInsight: Apply the rule directly: for each 1-indexed position that divides n, add the square of that element.

approaches.name: Direct loop over positions
approaches.summary: For i in 1..n, add nums[i - 1]^2 when n % i == 0.

approaches.name: Divisor pairs
approaches.summary: Enumerate d up to sqrt(n) and use both d and n // d.

personalSolution.approach: Loop over 0-indexed i and test n % (i + 1) == 0
personalSolution.notes: Optimal for n <= 50 and the index conversion is right.

canonicalCode:
class Solution:
    def sumOfSquares(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        total = 0
        for i in range(1, n + 1):          # 1-indexed position i, n <= 50
            if n % i == 0:                 # i divides n => nums[i] is special
                total += nums[i - 1] ** 2  # convert to the 0-indexed list
        return total
commonMistakes: Testing n % i with i starting at 0 (ZeroDivisionError).
Squaring the index instead of the element.

promptVariants: The problem is 1-indexed but Python lists are 0-indexed. Which loop body is correct for i in range(n)?
How do you test whether the element nums[i] (0-indexed) is special?
cards.explanation: The 1-indexed position of nums[i] is i + 1, so it is special when n % (i + 1) == 0 and its value is nums[i].

incorrectOptionExplanations.if n % i == 0: total += nums[i] ** 2: n % 0 raises ZeroDivisionError at i = 0, and the divisibility test uses the wrong position.
incorrectOptionExplanations.if n % (i + 1) == 0: total += nums[i + 1: That reads the next element and goes out of range on the last special index.
incorrectOptionExplanations.if n % i == 0: total += nums[i - 1] ** 2: i = 0 divides by zero; this form only works for i in range(1, n + 1).

promptVariants: Which elements are special for every array length?
Whatever n is, which two 1-indexed positions always divide n?
cards.explanation: 1 divides every n and n divides itself. For n = 1 these are the same element, counted once.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Positions 1 and 2: 2 divides n only for even n.
incorrectOptionExplanations.Positions n - 1 and n: n - 1 divides n only when n = 2 (or n = 1).

promptVariants: What is the time complexity of the canonical code?
Derive the running time from the loop.
cards.explanation: One loop over the n positions, each with a constant-time modulo and at most one multiplication.

incorrectOptionExplanations.O(sqrt(n)): That needs the divisor-pair trick; this loop tests every position.
incorrectOptionExplanations.O(n log n): There is no sorting or divide step.

promptVariants: Only a running total and the loop index are stored, so the extra space is O(___).
How could you visit only the special positions instead of testing all n?
Is there a faster way to enumerate the divisors of n?
cards.answer: Enumerate divisors in pairs: for d from 1 while d * d <= n, if n % d == 0 then both d and n // d are special (count d == n // d once). That is O(sqrt(n)) instead of O(n). With n <= 50 the simple loop is clearer and is what an interviewer expects.
keyPoints: Divisor pairs d and n // d
Do not double count a perfect square
cards.explanation: Know the faster option, and choose the simple one when the limits allow.
